name: PCX benchmarks
description: In this work, we tackle the problems of efficiency and scalability for predictive coding networks in machine learning. To do so, we first propose a library called PCX, whose focus lies on performance and simplicity, and provides a user-friendly, deep-learning oriented interface. Second, we use PCX to implement a large set of benchmarks for the community to use for their experiments. As most works propose their own tasks and architectures, do not compare one against each other, and focus on small-scale tasks, a simple and fast open-source library adopted by the whole community would address all of these concerns. Third, we perform extensive benchmarks using multiple algorithms, setting new state-of-the-art results in multiple tasks and datasets, as well as highlighting limitations inherent to PC that should be addressed. Thanks to the efficiency of PCX, we are able to analyze larger architectures than commonly used, providing baselines to galvanize community efforts towards one of the main open problems in the field: scalability. The code for PCX is available at \textit{https://github.com/liukidar/pcax}.
evaluation_method: accuracy and reconstruction_error (task-dependent; supervised tasks use accuracy, unsupervised tasks use reconstruction/error metrics)
general_score_metric: task-dependent (accuracy for supervised tasks; reconstruction error for unsupervised tasks)
reputation: A research-oriented benchmark suite for predictive coding networks; early-stage with limited but growing interest in the predictive-coding and theoretical ML communities.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark focused on predictive coding algorithms. Many tasks are research-scale; some results may be sensitive to implementation details and hyperparameter settings. Aims to improve scalability but may still contain small-scale legacy tasks.
